newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia Yield Spreads-Cruising towards parity.
newsitem.headline: Australia Yield Spreads-Cruising towards parity.

text.p: Australian bonds put in a strong outperformance against the U.S. after a weaker than expected employment report for June, breaching 35 basis points at one stage on the 10-year differential.
The market continues to make its steady voyage towards parity, spurred on by hopes of a further easing in monetary policy and striking levels not seen since 1981, analysts said.

The data, which saw total employment rise just 11,900 against forecasts for a rebound of over 40,000 and a further drop in full-time employment, has put the market back on alert for an easing, even as early as Friday.
However, an official rate cut from the current level of 5.5 percent is seen more likely after the inflation and wages data later this month, analysts added.

Since the middle of May this margin has dropped from around 100 basis points taking into account the last rate cut on May 23, a recent positive credit rating outlook by Moody's and amid uncertainty in the U.S. over whether the Federal Reserve will need to tighten policy again.

The three-year yield comparison to the U.S., which has been negative since just after the last local easing, was again nearing the minus 50 basis point level seen after the May labour force report released last month.
The market also outpaced Canada, but it lost some ground to the long end of the New Zealand curve after a well-received N.Z. bond tender of a new line of July 2009 stock.
